assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.

person_baseline.note: 200 of the people's own essays, each measured against the others the same way. A machine arm near this number is writing like the people; well above it is repeating them.

memorisation.note: The share of each essay's five-word sequences that also occur in the people's essays for this genre, measured against the whole human sample. Read it against person_baseline, not against zero: thousands of essays answering the same seven assignments share a great deal of ordinary phrasing, and a sentence invented for a test already matches about half the time. Well above the baseline is a model repeating writing it has seen.

essays.text:
Dear Principal,

I think that students should be required to perform community service. I know that some people might think it's taking away from their free time, but I believe that it's worth it. Not only does it help the community, but it also helps us students develop important skills.

For example, tutoring elementary school children can help them with their homework and understanding of certain subjects. This can not only help the children, but also give us students a chance to practice our communication and teaching skills. I've seen some of my friends who tutor make a real difference in the kids' lives, and it's something that we can all benefit from.

Additionally, cleaning up litter can help keep our community looking nice and clean. It's something that we can all be proud of, and it can also teach us responsibility and the importance of taking care of our environment. I've seen some of my friends who participate in this type of community service take great pride in their work and feel good about making a difference.

I know that some people might think that requiring community service is taking away from their free time, but I believe that it's worth it. We're lucky to have the opportunities that we do, and it's important that we give back to the community that gives us so much. Plus, it can be a great way to build friendships and learn new skills.

In conclusion, I think that requiring students to perform community service is a great idea. It can help us develop important skills, make a difference in our community, and give us a sense of pride and accomplishment. I would be happy to participate in community service and I think that it would be a valuable experience for all students.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

essays.text:
Dear Principal,

I think that students should not be required to perform community service. While I understand the importance of helping others and giving back to the community, I believe that forcing students to do it would not be effective. Many students already participate in community service voluntarily, and it's not because they are forced to. My friends who tutor elementary school children do it because they enjoy helping others and feel good about themselves after doing so. Similarly, my friends who clean up litter do it because they care about the environment and want to make a difference.

On the other hand, requiring students to do community service could have negative consequences. Some students may not have the time or energy to devote to community service, especially if they have heavy course loads or are involved in extracurricular activities. For example, my friend Emma has to take a heavy course load to get into her dream college, and she barely has time to finish her homework, let alone add community service to her schedule. Requiring her to do community service would only add to her stress and make it harder for her to succeed.

Another concern is that requiring community service could lead to superficial help that doesn't actually make a difference. For instance, if students are forced to clean up litter, they may not take the time to understand the root causes of pollution or find lasting solutions. Similarly, if students are forced to tutor elementary school children, they may not be able to develop meaningful relationships with their students or see the long-term impact of their efforts.

Instead of requiring community service, I think that our school should offer incentives and opportunities for students to participate voluntarily. For example, we could offer extra credit or special privileges for students who complete a certain number of hours of community service. We could also provide resources and support for students who want to start their own community service projects. This way, students can choose to participate in community service if they want to, and it won't add to their stress or affect their ability to succeed in school.

In conclusion, while community service is important, I don't think that students should be required to participate. Instead, I believe that our school should offer incentives and opportunities for students to participate voluntarily, and let them choose whether or not to get involved.
